title: Review: Radioactive decay: types and properties; Fundamental interactions and exchange particles; Particles, antiparticles and classification; Photons and the photoelectric effect; Pair production and annihilation; Conservation laws in particle interactions
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AQA A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: P01-uk2#t4 term and clue written for the game; P01-uk1#t2 term and clue written for the game; P02-2#t3 term and clue written for the game; P02-1#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: N02-uk2#N.4, P03-1#N.8, P05-1#N.2, Q01-1#N.4c, P03-1#N.3, P05-1#N.4, Q01-1#N.9a, P03-1#N.13a, P05-1#N.13, Q01-1#N.13, P03-1#N.11, P05-1#N.10. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Negative pion
items.clue: Meson made of a down quark and an anti-up quark, charge –1.

items.label: Baryon
items.clue: Particle made of three quarks, such as a proton or a neutron.

items.label: Beta-minus decay
items.clue: A down quark becomes an up quark, so a neutron becomes a proton.

items.label: Gravitational interaction
items.clue: Acts on all mass; infinite range; by far the feeblest of the four.

questions.stem: The chart shows neutron number N against proton number Z. Starting from the nucleus marked with a dot, four arrows (one of them a loop back to the same nucleus) are meant to show the change produced by each of the four types of decay, as labelled. One of the four is drawn incorrectly. Which one?
A student proposes that a free neutron decays into a proton and an electron and nothing else: n → p + e⁻. Which conservation law that holds in all nuclear decays would this proposal break?

options.text: Charge, since two charged particles would come from one neutral particle
Baryon number, since a neutron would be replaced by a proton
Lepton number, since the number of electrons and neutrinos would rise
Mass, since the proton and electron have less mass than the neutron

questions.stem: An electron and a positron annihilate, producing two photons. Which quantity is different after the annihilation from before it?
questions.explanation: Photons have no rest mass. The pair's mass has been converted to photon energy, but energy and momentum are conserved.

questions.stem: A laser pointer emits light of wavelength 633 nm with a power of 5.0 mW. How many photons does it emit each second? Use h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s and c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
In a decay, an up quark changes into a down quark. Which of these must also be emitted for charge to be conserved?
questions.explanation: +⅔ = −⅓ + 1 + 0. The quark loses one unit of charge, so a particle with +1e must leave: this is β⁺ decay.

questions.stem: A muon and an antimuon, both almost at rest, annihilate to produce two photons. The rest energy of a muon is 105.7 MeV. What is the wavelength of each photon?
Predict first. Which observation from photoelectric experiments cannot be explained by the classical wave theory of light?

options.text: Photoelectrons are emitted without any measurable delay, even in very dim light.
More photoelectrons are emitted each second when the light is made much more intense.
More photoelectrons are emitted each second when the frequency of the light is raised.
Every photoelectron leaves the metal with kinetic energy exactly hf minus the work function.

questions.stem: Which of these proposed interactions is forbidden by a conservation law?
questions.explanation: Q 0 = 0 and B 1 = 1, but L: 0 + 1 = +1 before, 0 − 1 = −1 after. Electron capture emits a neutrino, νₑ, not an antineutrino.

questions.stem: An electron and a positron, each with 0.30 MeV of kinetic energy, collide head-on and annihilate into two photons. The rest energy of an electron is 0.511 MeV. What is the energy of each photon?
questions.explanation: Head-on with equal energies, the total momentum is zero, so the two photons have equal energies and fly apart in opposite directions. Each: 0.511 + 0.30 = 0.81 MeV.

questions.stem: Light whose photons each have energy 4.0 eV shines on three metals: X, with work function 2.0 eV; Y, with work function 3.0 eV; and Z, with work function 4.5 eV. Which statement about the maximum kinetic energy of the electrons emitted from each metal is correct?

options.text: Z's electrons have the greatest maximum kinetic energy, and X's electrons the least
X's electrons have the greatest maximum kinetic energy, and Z emits no electrons
All three metals emit electrons, each with the same maximum kinetic energy
Their maximum kinetic energies cannot be ranked without the light's intensity

questions.stem: The Λ⁰ (quarks u, d, s) decays: Λ⁰ → p + π⁻. Which statement is correct?

options.text: It cannot happen, because strangeness is not conserved.
It is a strong interaction, because only hadrons take part.
It is a weak interaction: strangeness changes by +1.
It cannot happen, because baryon number changes.
